ai.literal: Luster having lost, dim-become eyes too; he departed days having counted-by-pressing worn-out fingers.
ai.translation: My eyes have lost their luster and grown dim looking for him; my fingers are worn thin from counting the days since he departed.
ai.modern: அவர் பிரிந்து சென்ற நாட்களைச் சுவரில் தொட்டுத் தொட்டு எண்ணியதால் என் விரல்கள் தேய்ந்து போயின; அவர் வரும் வழியைப் பார்த்துப் பார்த்து என் கண்களும் ஒளியிழந்து மங்கிவிட்டன.
ai.explanation: In this couplet, the heroine expresses the physical toll of her intense longing and waiting. Her eyes have lost their natural brightness (வாள்) and become dull (புற்கென்ற) from constantly watching the path for her lover's return. Meanwhile, her fingers (விரல்) have worn down (தேய்ந்த) from repeatedly touching and marking the wall (ஒற்றி) to count the days (நாள்) that have passed since he left (சென்ற). The imagery beautifully contrasts the passive strain of watching with the active, repetitive anxiety of counting time.

ai.literal: O shining jeweled one! Today if I forget, my shoulders upon ornaments will slip off, beauty having shed.
ai.translation: O wearer of shining jewels! If I try to forget him even for a single day, my shoulders will lose their beauty and the ornaments on them will slip off.
ai.modern: விளங்கும் அணிகலன்களை அணிந்த தோழியே! இன்று ஒருநாள் நான் அவரை மறக்க நினைத்தால், என் தோள்கள் தம் அழகை இழந்து, அவற்றின் மேல் உள்ள வளையல்களும் அணிகலன்களும் கழன்று விழுந்துவிடும்.
ai.explanation: In this couplet, the heroine speaks to her close friend who is adorned with bright jewels. She explains that she cannot afford to forget her beloved even for a single day to ease her pain. The moment she attempts to forget him, the grief of separation causes her body to waste away instantly. As her shoulders grow thin and lose their natural beauty (kārikai), the bracelets and ornaments (kalam) worn on them will lose their grip and slip off. This physical change serves as an immediate, visible sign of her deep yearning and the impossibility of forgetting him.

ai.literal: Willpower desiring, courage as companion, he who went; return desiring, still I exist.
ai.translation: Desiring strength of will, he departed with only his courage as a companion; desiring his return, I still cling to life.
ai.modern: மனவலிமையை விரும்பி, தன் நெஞ்சத்தையே துணையாகக் கொண்டு சென்ற காதலர் திரும்பி வருவதை விரும்பி, நான் இன்னும் உயிரோடு இருக்கிறேன்.
ai.explanation: The heroine speaks of her departed lover who left her to achieve a difficult task, driven by his strong willpower (உரன்) and accompanied only by his own courageous heart (உள்ளம்). Though his absence is painful, she explains that she keeps herself alive solely out of the intense desire (நசைஇ) to see him return (வரல்). The repetition of the word 'நசைஇ' (desiring) contrasts his desire for achievement with her desire for his return, highlighting the emotional tension between duty and love.

ai.literal: Thinking of the return of him who separated, my heart climbs to the peak, holding onto the love we enjoyed when united.
ai.translation: Thinking of the return of my departed lover, my heart climbs to the very peak of the love we once shared in union.
ai.modern: பிரிந்து சென்ற காதலரின் வருகையை நினைத்து, நாங்கள் ஒன்றுபட்டிருந்தபோது அனுபவித்த காதலைப் பற்றிக்கொண்டு என் நெஞ்சம் அதன் உச்சிக்கு ஏறிச் செல்கிறது.
ai.explanation: This couplet beautifully captures the heroine's intense anticipation of her lover's return. When she thinks of his homecoming, her heart does not merely wait; it actively climbs to the highest peak of the love they experienced when they were together. The word 'kōṭu' means a branch or a peak, and 'koṭu' is used here in the sense of holding onto something for support. Her heart uses the memory of their past united love as a branch to hold onto, climbing higher and higher into a state of ecstatic expectation.

ai.literal: May I see indeed the husband, eyes to be filled; having seen after, will depart my soft shoulders' pallor.
ai.translation: May I but behold my lord so that my eyes are filled with his sight; once I have seen him, the sallow pallor of separation will vanish from my soft shoulders.
ai.modern: என் கண்கள் குளிரும் வரை என் தலைவனை நான் காண்பேனாக! அவனைக் கண்ட பிறகு, என் மென்மையான தோள்களில் படர்ந்துள்ள பசலை நிறம் நீங்கிவிடும்.
ai.explanation: The heroine expresses her intense longing to gaze upon her lover, whom she addresses as the lord of the shore (கொண்கன்). She wishes to look at him until her eyes are completely satisfied (கண்ணார). She is certain that once she beholds him, the sickly yellow-green pallor (பசப்பு) that has spread over her soft shoulders (மென்தோள்) due to the pain of separation will instantly disappear.

ai.literal: Let come indeed my lord one day; I will drink [his presence] all distress-pain to perish.
ai.translation: Let my lord return for just a single day; I shall drink in his presence so that all this painful sorrow of separation vanishes.
ai.modern: என் தலைவன் ஒருநாள் மட்டும் வரட்டும்; என் துன்ப நோய் முழுவதும் அழியும்படி நான் அவனைக் கண்டு பருகுவேன்.
ai.explanation: In this verse, the heroine expresses her intense longing for her husband's return. She wishes for him to come back for just a single day, which she believes will be enough to cure her. She uses the vivid metaphor of 'drinking' (parukuvaṉ) to describe how eagerly and completely she will consume his presence. This feast of reunion will instantly banish all the painful affliction (paital nōy) caused by their long separation.

ai.literal: Shall I sulk? Or shall I embrace? Or shall I unite, when the husband who is like my eyes [is here]?
ai.translation: Shall I feign anger? Shall I embrace him? Or shall I immediately unite with him, now that my beloved husband, who is as precious as my own eyes, is here?
ai.modern: என் கண் போன்ற காதலராகிய என் கணவர் வரும்போது, நான் அவரிடம் ஊடல் கொள்வேனா? அல்லது அவரைத் தழுவுவேனா? அல்லது அவருடன் உடனே ஒன்றுபடுவேனா?
ai.explanation: The heroine is filled with intense excitement and sweet confusion upon the arrival of her beloved husband, who is as precious to her as her own eyes. She is caught in a dilemma of love, wondering whether she should first show feigned anger to punish him for his absence, immediately embrace him out of longing, or completely lose herself in union with him. The repeated use of the doubtful particles 'kol' and 'kollō' beautifully conveys her racing thoughts and the overwhelming rush of emotions she experiences.

ai.literal: Engaging in the task, may the king win and grant us release; uniting at home, we shall celebrate the evening as a feast.
ai.translation: May the king engage in his task and win, so that we may unite at home and celebrate the evening as a feast.
ai.modern: அரசன் தன் கடமையில் ஈடுபட்டு வெற்றி பெறட்டும்; நாம் நம் வீட்டில் ஒன்று கூடி, இந்த மாலைப் பொழுதை ஒரு விருந்தாகக் கொண்டாடுவோம்.
ai.explanation: The hero, who is away on a royal military campaign, eagerly wishes for the king to complete his task and achieve victory quickly. He longs to return to his wife so they can be reunited. In classical love poetry, the evening is usually a time of intense sorrow for separated lovers. However, the hero anticipates that once they unite at home, they will transform this dreaded evening into a joyous feast of reunion.

ai.literal: One day like seven days passes, to those who pine, reckoning the coming day of him who went to a far distance.
ai.translation: To those who pine, counting the days until the return of their beloved who has gone to a far country, a single day feels as long as seven.
ai.modern: தொலைதூரத்திற்குச் சென்ற காதலர் திரும்பி வரும் நாளைக் கணக்கிட்டு ஏங்குபவர்களுக்கு, ஒரு நாள் என்பது ஏழு நாட்களைப் போல மெதுவாகக் கழியும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet beautifully captures the agonizingly slow passage of time experienced by a pining lover. The speaker waits for her partner who has traveled to a distant land, constantly counting down the days until his promised return. In this state of intense longing, each single day feels as long as a whole week of seven days. The poet uses the simple contrast between 'one day' and 'seven days' to measure the psychological weight of separation.

ai.literal: If [I] obtain, what is the use? When [I] have obtained, what is the use? If [we] embrace, what is the use, when the heart, having broken, has wasted away?
ai.translation: What is the use of obtaining him, what is the use of having obtained him, and what is the use of embracing him, if my heart has already broken and wasted away?
ai.modern: தலைவனைப் பெற முடிந்தால் என்ன பயன்? பெற்றுவிட்டால் என்ன பயன்? கூடித் தழுவினால் என்ன பயன்? என் நெஞ்சம் உடைந்து அழிந்துபோன பிறகு?
ai.explanation: This couplet portrays the extreme grief of the heroine waiting for her lover. She feels that the prolonged separation has already shattered her heart beyond repair. She asks what purpose is served by getting him back, having him near, or even embracing him, if her inner self has already perished. The repetition of 'what is the use?' emphasizes her despair, showing that physical union loses all meaning once the emotional self is completely broken.
